content.comment_body: Hello, In another thread ([url]), the differences in hardware and measurement quality between both solutions were explained in detail. That discussion also included a sample configuration. My question now concerns the programming differences between using the [product_name] RTD module and the [product_name] AI module for temperature control. My assumption is that the [product_name] RTD module handles normalization internally, so additional normalization is not required. Can someone clarify the differences when programming these modules, and possibly provide a comparison example? A sample would be very helpful. Thank you.

Hello, The resolution of the standard [product_name] AI module is 1000 steps, which translates to 10mV per step. This level of precision is not sufficient for PT100/1000 sensors. For these types of sensors, higher resolution is needed to achieve acceptable measurement range and accuracy. Therefore, using PT100/1000 sensors is only practical if a transmitter converts the signal to 0...10V or 0/4...20mA, or when you use the [product_name] RTD module. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience difficulties configuring PT100/1000 temperature sensors, particularly when deciding between [product_name] RTD modules and standard AI modules. The main concern is that AI modules lack sufficient resolution for accurate readings, requiring workarounds or alternative hardware. The discussion underscores the need for clearer documentation and practical examples to help users select the appropriate configuration for reliable measurements.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek straightforward guidance for configuring PT100/1000 sensors with [product_name] RTD and AI modules. Ideally, users would like sample configurations and confirmation that normalization is managed internally by the RTD module for simplicity.
